thinking: Phase 1-6 analysis: Evaluating News/Media Alliance petitioning DOJ/FTC to probe Google spam policies. Stated goal: protect publishers from unfair de-ranking. Actual mechanism: leveraging regulatory pressure to extract search visibility rents and bypass algorithmic quality standards. Forces computed with high-resolution decimals; hypocrisy gap R_net=3.50 indicating partial distortion/opportunism.
subject: News/Media Alliance Calls on DOJ and FTC to Investigate Google’s Spam Policies | News/Media Alliance
posts:
News publishers demand DOJ and FTC probe Google's spam rules.
Evidence: NMA letter, EU/UK precedents, publisher traffic impacts
#TechPolicy #Antitrust

Google's spam policies unfairly penalize legitimate publisher content and require regulatory antitrust intervention.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

Publishers seek to immunize low-quality SEO practices and affiliate networks from algorithmic filtering under the guise of competition.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Publishers invoke antitrust protection to preserve revenue streams built on low-value aggregator content rather than organic user trust.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.5, z: 2)

- News/Media Alliance: COND (-0.5, -0.6) — Defending publisher revenues via state pressure.
- Google Spam Policy: COND (-0.6, -0.7) — Algorithmic enforcement with opaque collateral damage.
The News/Media Alliance petitioned US antitrust regulators to investigate Google's site reputation abuse policies, following similar regulatory scrutiny in the UK and EU.

The Poison:
Conflating legitimate investigative journalism with automated coupon aggregation and low-value affiliate SEO spam.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (algorithmic quality enforcement) with WHO (incumbent media revenue protection), treating commercial grievances as antitrust violations.

Social Physics Analysis:
Publishers run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, wrapping commercial revenue protection in the noble pretext of defending journalism to enlist state regulators against search algorithms.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Systemic friction increases as regulatory capture replaces algorithmic quality control.

The Unavoidable Truth: Search engines must filter spam to remain useful to consumers.

The Unavoidable Lie: All traffic drops on publisher sites represent anticompetitive censorship.

Alethekanon:
Regulators are weaponized as economic proxies when publishers fail to adapt to changing information markets. 🌐

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to watch local journalism struggle for survival, but using antitrust law to protect ad-stuffed coupon pages won't fix the underlying crisis of trust.

Brothekanon:
Media companies are just mad Google's spam filter caught their SEO link-farming tricks and tanked their referral traffic.

Spirithekanon:
"Wealth gained hastily will dwindle, but whoever gathers little by little will increase it." Proverbs 13.11 — PASS (Spiritual Vector)

aspects.reason: Weaponizing antitrust for SEO affiliate revenue protection.

Actual Article Body:

On October 7, the News/Media Alliance sent a letter to the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice to request the agencies open an investigation into Google’s anticompetitive conduct regarding its site reputation abuse policy. The letter addresses Google’s adoption and implementation of policies aimed at tackling “spammy, low-quality content on Search,” which Google has wielded as a sword to de-rank, and in some instances delist entirely, legitimate publisher properties. Many affected publisher websites provide valuable editorial material, coupons and other promotional material to millions of American consumers, that provide American businesses an efficient way to attract new and retain existing customers through affiliate partnerships.

In its letter, NMA calls on US authorities to examine Google’s practices following the United Kingdom and the European Union’s recent successful efforts to limit Google’s unfair application of these policies. The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority recently introduced conduct requirements on Google related to fair ranking, anti-discrimination, advance notice, and enhanced appeals frameworks for penalized publishers. Google, meanwhile, announced that manual actions issued under its Site Reputation Abuse Policy would not be applied within the European Economic Area following discussions with the European Commission.  The Commission had previously initiated an investigation into Google’s application of the Site Reputation Abuse Policy. NMA urges similar regulatory focus in the US, so that US publishers are protected at the same level as European businesses.  Read the full letter here.

Ken Paxton calls out James Talarico's 11-day absence at Trump rally, prompting response from campaign

Ken Paxton led a "Where is Talarico?" chant at Trump's San Antonio rally, but James Talarico's campaign says the Democrat has been sick with the flu.

The Texas attorney general questioned his Democratic Senate rival's whereabouts during President Trump's San Antonio rally, saying Talarico had not been seen campaigning in the state for 11 days.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton questioned Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico's absence from the campaign trail during President Donald Trump's rally in San Antonio Wednesday, prompting a response from his opponent's campaign less than a month before the November midterm elections.

Paxton led the crowd in chanting "Where is Talarico?" while asserting that the Democrat had not been seen campaigning in Texas for 11 days.

Talarico's campaign told Fox News Digital the Democrat has been sick with the flu and is expected to return to the campaign trail this weekend.

PAXTON VENTS OVER LACK OF CAMPAIGN CONTROL AS DC ESTABLISHMENT HE ONCE BATTLED COMES TO HIS AID

President Donald Trump, left, listens as Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton speaks during a campaign rally at Freeman Coliseum in San Antonio Oct. 7, 2026. (Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)

"After holding more than 100 public events and shaking tens of thousands of hands, James came down with the flu but will be back on the trail this weekend," JT Ennis, a campaign spokesperson for Talarico, told Fox News Digital.

"Ken Paxton has been ignoring Texans this entire campaign, and his priorities are clear: He doesn’t answer to the people of this state. He answers to his billionaire megadonors and special interests."

The statement from Talarico campaign spokesperson JT Ennis also criticized Paxton's campaign priorities, pushing back against the Republican's remarks as the two candidates compete for a U.S. Senate seat.

Trump also questioned Talarico's whereabouts during his remarks, repeatedly referencing the Democrat's absence while campaigning on Paxton's behalf.TRUMP-LINKED MAGA INC POURS $10M INTO KEN PAXTON'S TEXAS SENATE RACE AGAINST JAMES TALARICO

President Donald Trump watches a video during a campaign rally at Freeman Coliseum in San Antonio Oct. 7, 2026. Trump visited Texas to campaign for Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

The president suggested without evidence that Talarico had become sick after eating meat for political reasons, mocking the Democrat's dietary preferences.

Trump also criticized Talarico's positions on immigration, public safety and education, while praising Paxton's record as Texas attorney general and urging voters to support his Senate bid.

The president emphasized the importance of the Texas race to Republicans' efforts to maintain control of Congress, warning supporters about the consequences of Democrats gaining seats in the Senate.

MEET THE VOTERS WHO COULD BREAK THE GOP’S DECADESLONG GRIP ON A REPUBLICAN STRONGHOLD

Democrat candidate for U.S. Senate James Talarico speaks during a rally in San Antonio, Texas, May 29, 2026. (Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images)

Trump's appearance in San Antonio was part of a broader effort to mobilize Republican voters ahead of the midterm elections. He urged attendees to participate in early voting, which begins Oct. 19 in Texas, or cast their ballots on Election Day.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The exchange over Talarico's whereabouts comes as the candidates enter the final weeks of the campaign.
